question: A 19-year-old Caucasian male collapsed from sudden cardiac arrest while playing in a college basketball game. Attempts at resuscitation were unsuccessful. Post-mortem pathologic and histologic examination found asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial disarray. Assuming this was an inherited condition, the relevant gene most likely affects which of the following structures?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy -> myocardial disarray -> inherited condition -> affects cardiac cell sarcomere proteins -> 80% CHAIN: Sudden cardiac arrest -> post-mortem examination -> inherited condition -> affects membrane potassium channel proteins -> 75% CHAIN: Collapsed during basketball game -> post-mortem findings -> inherited condition -> affects ryanodine receptors -> 80%
enhanced_information: The relevant gene most likely affects cardiac cell sarcomere proteins, leading to asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial disarray in this case of sudden cardiac arrest during a basketball game. The evidence paths do not provide direct support for the other options.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), a genetic condition that commonly affects cardiac cell sarcomere proteins. The presence of asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial disarray aligns with the typical features of HCM. The enhanced information provided further supports this by indicating that the relevant gene most likely affects cardiac cell sarcomere proteins. Other options like membrane potassium channel proteins, ryanodine receptors, autoimmune beta-cell antibodies, and membrane sodium channels are not directly associated with the characteristic findings of HCM in this context.
